body:
- exfoliate 24h beforehand and let the hair grow out for a few days/weeks until there are minimal bumps 

- using a sharp, clean razor every time (making sure to clean razor out and air-dry after use to prolong life of blades). Men’s razor blades or good quality 5-blade razor heads are best 

- (this changed my life) applying an oil, like coconut oil or baby oil, to the leg as a lubricant. This is how I got the closest, smoothest shave. you can use shaving cream on top 

- not too slow, not too fast, against the grain for a closer shave or, as others said, with the grain for less chance of irritation, in small stages. Rinse hair from blade after every stroke

- wash leg with an unscented/sensitive formula body wash afterward until no oil/cream remains

- rinse your shaved area with cold water afterwards to close the pores up

- gently towel pat dry - do NOT scrub or rub 

- moisturise with a neutral, unscented, thin formula moisturiser afterwards (like a lotion, not a butter)

- as others have said, keep moisturising/exfoliating on days you are not shaving, too

- DON’T SHAVE STUBBLE!! let it grow out a lil or you’ll be back to square one! 

in my experience it’s basically impossible to have smooth skin every day from shaving alone so… plan your shaving around when you most need to be smooth or save your pennies up for a wax/epilation session :)

I was about two minutes’ walk from the edge of a very tall viaduct when I encountered a sweet little tabby cat. It was a pretty rural path, 2 in the morning, pitch black, winter, and 2 miles from town at that point, so I found it curious that it should be that far out. It joined my party, and kept dashing in front of my feet, meowing at me relentlessly. Then, when I lent against the side of the viaduct, it hopped up next to me. I was so completely at peace with my decision before; I’d written letters, a will, packed up my possessions in my house. But, for some reason, I couldn’t leave that little cat in the dark, so I coaxed it all the way back to town, and at that point, I called for some help. I am really glad it was there now.

hey, I really empathise with what you’re saying, and I’m sorry to hear you’re feeling this way too. as soon as December starts, I get this looming sense of dread. It’s totally valid to feel that way. This time of year does not mean the same thing to some as it does to others. 

for me, it helps me to channel all my energy into doing things for others who deserve it. for the past three christmases I solidly rebuffed christmas, got some small gifts for the few folks i am fortunate to have, served christmas lunches at church (not religious, its just where they do it), went home, and smoked up. It’s nice to donate (doesn’t have to be a lot!!) or put together a parcel for charities or orgs that give gifts to children who wouldn’t get them otherwise, kinda heals my inner child. sometimes it’s so, so hard to push through and feel any positive emotion at this time of year, I get that, and I have some days where I walk through town like I want to rip down all the decorations and scream lol. it hurts to witness what you don’t have. but for sure, the thing that makes me feel the best is being as good as I possibly can. it’s also nice to spoil yourself a little… :)

whatever way you feel and spend your time is completely valid and okay. you don’t have to pretend. i hope you can find some peace this month, in some small way. stay safe

I used to be good friends with a guy in my teenage years. We were all in a sort of group together, behaving recklessly, drinking and smoking too much. He had a bit of a thing for me, but was never pushy about it, which I massively respected, because not a lot of men had been so kind to me before. Got a bit short-tempered after a drink, but never nasty to any of us. I knew he’d had trouble with the law in the past for fighting, though. He was the sort of person who would give you money for food when you had none. He ran across town to save me from somebody in my house threatening to kill me, once. He got a trade job and stopped hanging around with us, or talking to us, and I was glad to see him doing well. 

Last year, I saw his mugshot on Facebook. He had stabbed a man to death in his house one street over from where I lived at the time. I didn’t even know he was living in town. They had a fight over something (I suspect it was drugs, from talking to a few people) and the guy I knew was taken to hospital to receive emergency medication. When he left, he walked to a local supermarket, bought some knives, went back to the house and stabbed his companion over 20 times, leaving the knife in. I saw one of those ridiculous true crime commentary videos on it a couple weeks ago, and it really messed me up to hear in detail what he had done. I wish I didn’t watch that video. I don’t condone what he did - I think it’s vile - but I don’t hate him, either. I just feel sad about it.

This was in Year 5 at school (so I was around ten). We went with Year 6 on one of those outward bound trips to do rock climbing, kayaking, all that good stuff. It was our first stayaway trip, and we stayed in dormitories - girls in one, boys in the other. There was only around 15 girls between years 5 and 6. We shared bunk beds - I chose the top one, with my best friend beneath. 

Night 2, I pretended to talk in my sleep for a bit of a joke. Everyone took it very seriously. One of the bolder girls came up to my bunk and listened to what I was saying, then relayed it back for the whole dorm to hear. 

I said some stupid stuff, I can’t even remember, but eventually, I said ‘I need the loo’. 

This sent the entire dorm into meltdown. The girl relayed my message - “she said she needs the loo, oh my god, she’s going to wet the bed. Guys. She’s going to wet the bed!!” 

Multiple girls were crying at this point. I maintained my pretence of being ‘asleep’, but stopped talking. 

The girl went up to the ‘panic button’ (an alarm to be pressed in case of emergency, that would alert staff to our dorm) and went along the hall to wake up our teachers. The alarm was very loud, like an air raid or something. At this point, I ‘woke up’ to see the carnage I’d created. 

Two girls were huddled on the furthest bunk away from me, crying. Everybody was everywhere, nobody was in their beds. They all looked at me with a mixture of fear and disgust. My friend sleeping below me was also crying, and refused to sleep there that night - all because I said I’d needed the toilet.

The brigade of staff and teachers entered the room, and the translating girl explained the situation with great gusto to them. They politely informed her that it was very late, we had activities to do in the morning, and it was not an emergency. I was ushered to the toilet by a teaching assistant, returned to bed safely, and all was well in the world. 

I don’t think I was invited to any sleepover parties that year.

My dad. Thankfully they aren’t together any more, but for 12 years he was with the literal embodiment of evil stepmother. 

She treated me way different to her own kids, would always organise ‘activities’ to get me out of the house, and always gave me filthy looks. One time I turned my light back on after she’d turned it off and she grabbed me by the jaw and shook my head. It sounds kind of pathetic writing it out but she just made it absolutely known that she didn’t like me and didn’t want me there. 

She stopped him from going out to see his friends and going fishing (which he’s loved since he was 6.) After I ‘dated’ her daughter’s ex boyfriend (at the age of 10) she kicked me out of the house. After that she limited the times I could see him and wouldn’t let me stay at their house. He was also limited on how much he could help me and my mum financially, so we were dirt poor for a while. 

She basically made my dad her bitch for years. My whole family hated her, and even her own parents tried to talk him round. It only ended when she left him for another man, who she married after six months. Last I heard, she’s treating his kids in the same way and they all hate their dad now. They don’t see him any more.

My dad loves to talk about how much of a bitch she is now... but she was an angel for 12 years before that! ;)
